html:
The Ngarluma are an Aboriginal Australian people of the western Pilbara coast of Western Australia, around Roebourne and Karratha. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815. Their language forms a dialect chain with that of the Kariyarra to the east.

Their other neighbours were the Martuthunira to the west and the Yindjibarndi inland. Roebourne, founded in 1866, was the first European town of the northwest, and sheep stations and pearling quickly drew Ngarluma people into hard and often forced labour. Nearby, on the Burrup Peninsula, settlers killed many of the Yaburara people in the Flying Foam massacre of 1868.

The Burrup, or Murujuga, holds one of the largest collections of rock engravings in the world, and the Ngarluma are among its custodians. In 2005 a court recognised their native title together with the Yindjibarndi.
